plain_description.what: Questions were grouped into k-means cells at about 25, 50, 100, 200 and 400 cells. The routing gain at each size was measured on held-out data. No calls were made.
plain_description.why: It asks whether there is a best number of cells for model profiles, and whether finer cells route better than coarse ones.
plain_description.information: A clear peak at a middle size would identify the right granularity. Coarse cells winning would mean fine cells add nothing. Result: done, descriptive only. A best middle granularity is not shown. 100 cells beat 25 by +0.69 points, but the interval crosses 0. 100 cells beat 400 by +1.55 points (interval above zero), but this is not read as over-splitting: with 400 cells each cell's estimate rests on fewer questions and is noisier. The choice of 100 as best was itself noisy. Coarse cells did not win. The result is source-conditioned.
